newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Rubin urges Vietnam to press on with reform.
newsitem.headline: Rubin urges Vietnam to press on with reform.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Monday urged Vietnam to press ahead quickly with its economic reforms, saying that would lead the way to closer ties between the two former war-time foes.
"There is a lot Vietnam can do -- and do quickly," Rubin said in a speech to the U.S.-Vietnam Trade Council here.

Rubin, the highest-ranking U.S. economic official to visit Vietnam since the end of the war in 1975, ticked off a list of measures that Hanoi could take to mobilise its private sector and attract foreign investment.

Among the measures he advocated were lower trade tariffs, the elimination of import licences, the streamlining of government licensing requirements, modernisation of land laws and enhanced protection of intellectual property rights.
"Further progress in reform will ... open the door for closer economic ties between our two governments," Rubin said.

The Treasury chief, who earlier signed a $145 million debt rescheduling agreement with his Vietnamese counterpart said that his visit signified a shift in the bilateral relationship from conflict to cooperation.

The next step would be a trade agreement between the two countries but in order for that to come about, Vietnam must make "substantial commitments" to open up its markets and treat foreign companies the same as Vietnamese ones, he said.
He said that the United States has presented a draft trade agreement to Vietnam. The two countries are scheduled to resume negotiations on that front later this month.

The conclusion of a trade pact would help Vietnam become eligible for Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trade privileges and financing from the United States, Rubin said. MFN guarantees non-discriminatory tariffs on exports.
But Rubin added Hanoi would need to take additional steps to secure that.
"For example, if Vietnam wants access to OPIC (Overseas Private Investment Corp) loans and insurance programmes, Vietnam will need to satisfy fair labour standards," he said.
